stances.claim: Carpio's three declined nominations are best understood as expressions of 'delicadeza' rather than indecision -- the first because he dissented from the Court's authorization of GMA's midnight CJ appointment (his former client); the third because he dissented from the Sereno ouster, opining the Court had no power to oust its members; and the fifth because accepting would have made him 'Mr. One-Day Chief Justice.'

The saddest of the five missed chances was 2012: after Corona's impeachment, P-Noy reportedly told Carpio he was 'most qualified and most senior' but could not be chosen because some Senate allies and three businessmen opposed him -- a denial CJ separately verified.

Carpio's consuming ambition at this point is 'his passionate crusade for the sovereign rights of our country in the West Philippine Sea' -- making titles, honors, and testimonials secondary to substance.

Carpio is the longest-serving associate justice (18 years), second only to first CJ Cayetano Arellano (19 years from 1901-1920) -- and his eight months of acting-CJ service exceed the titled tenures of De Castro (<2 months), Pedro L. Yap (<3 months), and Jose Abad Santos (<4 months).

Carpio is 'a man of deep convictions and enormous moral courage... guided by basic values like integrity, honor, patriotism and accountability... hates forked tongues, two-faced Januses, grafters, and schemers' -- and 'it is more important to be correct and to be honor-bound than to be titled grandiosely and to be damned in history.'

notable_anecdotes: Carpio's quip explaining his first decline: 'I do not want to be known as Mr. Midnight Chief Justice.'

The post-Corona 2012 phone call: 'On his way home from the Palace, he called me, sadly saying, The President told me that he had no doubts about my qualifications... However, he could not appoint me because some of his key Senate allies and three prominent business leaders opposed my promotion.'
Lucio Singh's tip that Duterte was open to elevating Carpio for 'at least a day or two' before his compulsory retirement -- declined to avoid the 'Mr. One-Day Chief Justice' title.

Carpio's refusal of the traditional special-session retirement ceremony at the hallowed session hall, preferring a 'simple dinner with his colleagues and close friends at the Conrad Hotel' -- and the Court's unanimous resolution (Carpio taking no part) granting him CJ-level retirement benefits.
The reprised 60th-birthday toast as the column's closing tribute, with 'Mabuhay!' as the sign-off -- a CJ-signature register marker.

one_paragraph_summary: Marking Senior Justice Antonio T. Carpio's retirement on Oct 26, 2019 upon his 70th birthday, Panganiban catalogues his five missed chances to become Chief Justice across 18 years on the Court. The first (May 17, 2010, post-CJ Puno) Carpio declined out of 'delicadeza' because he had voted against the Court's decision authorizing former client GMA's midnight CJ appointment -- 'I do not want to be known as Mr. Midnight Chief Justice.' The second (May 29, 2012, post-Corona ouster) he accepted; on his way home from a Malacañang interview, he sadly called CJ Panganiban to report that P-Noy said he was 'most qualified and most senior' but could not appoint him because of opposition from Senate allies and three businessmen (CJ later separately verified all the named opponents' denials). The third (May 11, 2018, post-Sereno removal) Carpio declined out of 'delicadeza' because he had dissented from the ouster decision, opining the Court had no power to oust its members. The fourth (Oct 10, 2018, post-De Castro) he accepted, but Duterte chose Bersamin (the third most senior). The fifth (Oct 18, 2019, post-Bersamin) Carpio declined his automatic JBC nomination -- even though Lucio Singh told CJ that Duterte was open to elevating him for at least a day or two -- because acceptance would have made him 'Mr. One-Day Chief Justice.' His consuming ambition now is 'his passionate crusade for the sovereign rights of our country in the West Philippine Sea.' He is the longest-serving associate justice (18 years, second only to first CJ Cayetano Arellano's 19 years), and his eight months of acting-CJ service exceed the titled tenures of De Castro (<2 months), Pedro L. Yap (<3 months), and Jose Abad Santos (<4 months). The Court unanimously (Carpio taking no part) granted him CJ-level retirement benefits, after he declined the traditional retirement ceremony in favor of a simple dinner with colleagues and close friends at the Conrad Hotel. CJ closes by reprising his 60th-birthday toast: Carpio is 'a man of deep convictions and enormous moral courage... it is more important to be correct and to be honor-bound than to be titled grandiosely and to be damned in history. Mabuhay!'
